clue.text: Boy meets girl — a divine system!

parts.note: Theo is a boy's name, short for Theodore
Sophy is a girl's name, a form of Sophie

explanation.surface: An excited announcement that a romantic boy-meets-girl story amounts to a religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meets' simply joins the two names side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystical philosophy claiming direct insight into God is exactly a religious doctrine of this kind.

clue.text: Teach trout to swim

indicators.note: swimming moves the letters of trout about into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to train a fish to swim.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct someone privately is to coach them.

clue.text: Avengers of Ireland? Correct

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
yes is the reply meaning 'that is correct'

explanation.surface: A question whether some Irish avengers exist, answered in the affirmative.
explanation.walkthrough: These are the Furies of Greek myth, who punished wrongdoers.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Furies pursued and punished crimes, so they were divine avenging spirits.

clue.text: Tassel on hilt didn't go up very far, we hear

indicators.note: the phrase is what we hear spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: 'soared not' means did not fly up high

explanation.surface: Someone says that a sword's tassel did not rise very high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soared not' said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of ribbon tied to a sword's grip is a decorative cord of this kind.

clue.text: Such times didn't make records

parts.note: suggests music that never charted, but means ages before writing, when nobody kept any written account

explanation.surface: A remark about years when no hit discs were made.
explanation.definitionFit: The ages before written history began left no written documents.

clue.text: Hear why Moses wrote

parts.note: the letter heard as 'why', written in the Hebrew alphabet of Moses

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be told the reason Moses put pen to paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'why' sounds like the letter Y; the Hebrew letter for that sound is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet corresponds to the English letter Y.

clue.text: Place where voracious creature stops before finishing

indicators.note: the word stops short of its final letter, so its last letter is cut off

parts.note: a locust is a famously greedy insect that strips crops bare

explanation.surface: A hungry animal pauses in the middle of its meal at some spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops before finishing' cuts the final T from LOCUST.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin and in mathematics a locus is a position or site.

clue.text: Abandon holiday

definitions.meaning: to quit or desert a place or person

explanation.surface: Someone deserts their holiday plans.
explanation.definitionFit: To go away from or desert, and also authorised time off from work.

clue.text: Bad temper a result of foul drink, perhaps

parts.note: choler is an old word for anger or irritability

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper after a disgusting drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The disease spreads through contaminated water, so drinking it is one cause.
explanation.definitionFit: This infectious bowel disease is caught from contaminated drinking water.

clue.text: A winning margin — others had to struggle

indicators.note: struggling throws the letters of 'others had' into disorder

explanation.surface: The winner only scraped home while the rest battled.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing the smallest winning distance is less than a head's length.

clue.text: Hated interval of working in common

indicators.note: the word for working is placed inside the word for common

parts.note: trite means commonplace, hackneyed
on means switched on, operating

explanation.surface: Someone loathed a break spent doing chores together.
explanation.walkthrough: The augmented fourth was nicknamed 'the devil in music' and avoided by medieval composers, hence 'hated'. 'Interval' is musical, not a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical gap of three whole tones, the diabolus in musica, was shunned by early church composers.

clue.text: Native seen in back-to front smelly top

indicators.note: the native is seen inside the turned word for smelly
the word for smelly is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: olid is an old word meaning foul-smelling
Abo is a dated, now offensive, word for an Aboriginal Australian

explanation.surface: An indigenous person spotted wearing a malodorous shirt put on the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-front' turns the smelly word into DILO. 'top' looks like a garment but is the spinning toy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a juggling toy spun on a string between two sticks, a kind of spinning toy.

clue.text: Beamed? Yes, in a way

indicators.note: the word for yes sits inside the abbreviation for a way

parts.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way
aye is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they smiled broadly replies, after a fashion, that they did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beamed' suggests smiling; here it means sending out rays, and the question mark flags the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Having or giving out rays of light is to be beamed in the sense of radiating.

clue.text: New Pope following one that is without mercy

indicators.note: the new Pope comes after the one, so it follows the letter for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Clement was the name of fourteen popes

explanation.surface: A freshly elected pontiff succeeds a predecessor who was merciless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts N CLEMENT after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement is a formal word for harsh or unmerciful, now mostly said of severe weather.

clue.text: Move last of tourists to so-called holiday resort

indicators.note: moving the letters about rearranges them
the final letter of the word tourists is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to shift the remaining visitors to a resort with a fancy name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of tourists' is S; with TO SO-CALLED that gives eleven letters that 'Move' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain's southern Mediterranean coastline is a popular seaside holiday area.

clue.text: Laughing, perhaps, and boasting

definitions.meaning: laughing ..., nitrous oxide, is one example of this
empty bragging talk is called this in informal speech

explanation.surface: Someone is giggling and bragging at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrous oxide is the laughing kind of vapour, and idle bragging is informally hot air of the same name.

clue.text: Rock to wedge top of rickety table

parts.note: a gib is a wedge or tapered metal bar used to hold parts in place

indicators.note: the first letter of rickety, the top in a down clue

parts.note: an altar is the communion table in a church

explanation.surface: Advice to steady a wobbly table by wedging a stone under it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' is the nickname of the British territory at the tip of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The British territory at the mouth of the Mediterranean is known as the Rock after its limestone peak.

clue.text: Absolutely nothing different from a custom

parts.note: 'not as' means unlike, different from
a usage is an established custom or practice

explanation.surface: A claim that some habit is utterly unlike any custom at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces as 'not as a usage', i.e. different from a custom. The answer is British slang for nothing whatsoever.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang phrase means not even the smallest thing, zero.

clue.text: A French king about this time was innocent

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the word for king goes round the phrase meaning this time

parts.note: taken as written
now means at this time

explanation.surface: A French monarch of this era was naive.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'A' at the start, which the held text dropped; UN, French for 'a', starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking awareness or knowledge means being naive, unaware of what is going on.

clue.text: After problem with heel, scrum may secure little possession

indicators.note: the scrum comes after the heel problem in the answer

parts.note: a blister is a sore often rubbed up on the heel by a shoe
in rugby the forwards forming a scrum are called the pack

explanation.surface: Rugby talk: after a heel injury, the scrum wins little of the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby surface ('heel', 'scrum', 'possession') hides packaging: a plastic bubble on card holding a small item.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear plastic bubbles on card hold small goods such as pills or batteries, keeping a little item safe.

clue.text: Carving gets 50% bigger in one month

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the half word goes inside one month

parts.note: May is a month of the year

indicators.note: half of the word bigger, its second half

explanation.surface: A sculpture grows half as large again during a single month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carving' means carved figures, an old sense, not the act of cutting; '50%' keeps the back half of the word bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: Carved figures or images collectively, an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Old character died in disgrace — his name?

parts.note: mu is a letter of the ancient Greek alphabet
d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone of old died disgraced, and we ask what he was called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his name?' points to the idiom 'his name is mud', said of someone in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dragged through dirt is a stock image of shame, as in the idiom about a disgraced person's name.

clue.text: Depressing weekend thought in the rainy season?

definitions.meaning: the gloomy Sunday-night reflection that Monday is coming shortly
the seasonal wind of South Asia brings heavy rain

explanation.surface: A gloomy weekend reflection during wet weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Asian seasonal wind brings months of heavy rain, and split as 'Mon soon' it is a weekend lament.

clue.text: Dangerous fall of a curtain Henry trapped

indicators.note: Henry is caught inside the curtain, so his letter goes within it

parts.note: a valance is a short curtain or drape round a bed or above a window
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry is caught beneath a curtain that falls on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped' puts H inside VALANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow sliding down a mountain is a perilous descent.

clue.text: A price for South Pacific feature

parts.note: a toll is a charge or price paid, as for a road

explanation.surface: A fee to see the musical South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics suggest the musical, but the definition is a ring-shaped coral island in that ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon is a common sight in that ocean.

clue.text: One admitting the holder

definitions.meaning: to own up is to admit, so one who owns in that sense admits something
the possessor of something holds it

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being the person keeping the item.
explanation.definitionFit: To own can mean to confess, and a possessor is someone who holds property.

clue.text: Plunder is widespread when money is locked up

indicators.note: the money is shut inside the word for widespread

parts.note: rife means prevalent, widespread
L is the abbreviation for pound, libra, money

explanation.surface: Looting is common when cash is kept in vaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locked up' puts L inside RIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack or search through and steal is to loot.

clue.text: Small purchase to keep after end of sale

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for keep comes after the letter from sale
the final letter of the word sale is taken

parts.note: to hold is to keep

explanation.surface: A shopper wants a reserved item kept back until the sale finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of sale' gives E; 'after' puts HOLD behind it. 'purchase' means a grip, not something bought.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber's small foothold gives a slight grip, and purchase means a firm hold.

clue.text: It's no good — lots of these are worn

definitions.meaning: a failure, something useless or a bomb that does not explode
in the plural it is slang for clothes

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a common wearable item is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A useless thing is a failure, and in the plural the word is slang for clothes.

clue.text: Incidental benefit of bowling the other way round

indicators.note: the two halves of the bowling term swap places, front part to the back

parts.note: off spin is a style of slow bowling in cricket that turns the ball from the off side

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: delivering the ball turning the opposite way brought an unexpected advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other way round' moves OFF from the front of OFFSPIN to the end. Off spin is a cricket bowling style.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary product or advantage arising from something else is a by-product of this kind.

clue.text: Beheading — fairly rough and ready in Arabia

indicators.note: rough means roughly made, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the head, or first letter, of the following word is removed

explanation.surface: A beheading in Arabia carried out in a crude, hasty fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beheading' cuts F from FAIRLY, leaving AIRLY; 'rough' rearranges it. 'ready' is slang for cash, as in 'the readies'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the currency unit of Saudi Arabia and Qatar, so it is cash there.

clue.text: Working assiduously with coach

definitions.meaning: the noun means steady careful effort, the quality of working hard
a public stagecoach in France was called by this name

explanation.surface: Someone is studying hard together with their trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady hard work is industriousness, and a French stagecoach was a public carriage of the same name.
